content: Ina May Gaskin is a Certified Professional Midwife (CPM) who has been referred to as the mother of authentic midwifery. In 1971, she and her husband, Stephen, established The Farm, a renowned intentional community located in Summertown, Tennessee. At The Farm, Gaskin and her team of midwives created one of the first out-of-hospital birth centers in the United States. The birthing practices at The Farm adhere to the recommendations of the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG). Family members and friends are often present during births and are encouraged to actively participate in the process. The significance of Gaskin's work is profound. According to Carol Lorente (1995), the impact of her contributions, along with those of The Farm midwives, was amplified by the publication of her book Spiritual Midwifery in 1977. Gaskin is credited with the rise and popularization of direct-entry midwifery in the United States, beginning in the early 1970s. She is also the publisher of the periodical Birth Gazette and an internationally recognized speaker on maternity care issues. She has represented the Midwives Alliance of North America (MANA) at various events, including the Starwood Festival and the WinterStar Symposium, where she has discussed the history and importance of midwifery. Additionally, she founded the Safe Motherhood Quilt Project, a national initiative aimed at raising awareness about maternal mortality rates and honoring women who have died from pregnancy-related causes over the past two decades. Her book Ina May's Guide to Childbirth was published in 2003. A study conducted by Durand in 1992 examined the outcomes of 1,707 home births attended by The Farm midwives in rural Tennessee between 1971 and 1989. These outcomes were compared to over 14,000 physician-attended hospital births in 1980. The study analyzed perinatal deaths, labor complications, and the use of assisted delivery. It concluded that, under certain conditions, home births attended by lay midwives can be as safe as, and involve fewer interventions than, physician-attended hospital deliveries. Ina May Gaskin has delivered lectures at midwifery conferences and medical schools worldwide. She served as the President of the Midwives Alliance of North America from 1996 to 2002. Her accolades include the ASPO/Lamaze Irwin Chabon Award (1997) and the Tennessee Perinatal Association Recognition Award. In 1997, she was also named a Visiting Fellow of Morse College at Yale University. Her bibliography includes the following works: Babies, Breastfeeding & Bonding (1987, Bergin & Garvey Publishers, ISBN 0-89789-134-1) Spiritual Midwifery (2002, The Book Publishing Company, ISBN 1-57067-104-4; originally published in 1977) Ina May's Guide to Childbirth (2003, Bantam, ISBN 0-553-38115-6) She has also authored several articles, including: Induced and Seduced: The Dangers of Cytotec, published in Mothering (July-August 2001) The Undervalued Art of Vaginal Breech Birth: A Skill Every Birth Attendant Should Learn, published in Mothering (July-August 2004) A Summary of Articles Published in English about Misoprostol (Cytotec) for Cervical Ripening or Induction of Labor, published online in 2005 Ina May Gaskin's work has been widely recognized and celebrated for its contributions to midwifery and maternal care.
